ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p182/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p182/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p182/r1.claim: Brief reminders about creation, life’s sources, death, and resurrection expose the transience of arrogant pride and point to Judgment.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p182/r1.anchor: In these verses, the pride and vanity of these people is condemned

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p184/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p184/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p184/r1.claim: Judgment will evaluate people’s good and evil deeds, select those who meet its standards, and cast down those who fail them.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p184/r1.anchor: evaluates the good and evil done by him

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p184/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p184/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p184/r2.claim: God’s measuring, planning, and easing of human creation and life stages show providence has a purpose, which entails judgment and recompense.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p184/r2.anchor: it is essential that a day come wherein it judges him

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p184/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p184/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p184/r3.claim: The relevant term describes life’s gradual stages from childhood through youth to old age; like the moon’s phases in 36:39, these attest to divine power and purposeful creation, resurrection, and judgment.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p184/r3.anchor: this word directs our attention to the various stages of life through which he gradually passes

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p409/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p409/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p409/r2.claim: God's determination in the womb includes body, appearance, height, and felicity or misery; another view describes development from drop to embryo.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p409/r2.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: أي في بطن أمه، وعنه قدر أعضاءه، وحسنا ودميما

BIQAI-FULL:v8p322#s080/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p322#s080/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p322#s080/r1.claim: The surah explains the call to warn those who fear by using resurrection to purify receptive hearts; human creation and the cycle of food prove God’s power, making rejection astonishing.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p322#s080/r1.anchor: بأن المراد الأعظم تزكية القابل للخشية بالتخويف بالقيامة

RAZI-FULL:v31p55#3/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p55#3/r1.speaker: الفراء
RAZI-FULL:v31p55#3/r1.claim: Al-Farrāʾ says God apportioned the human through stages from drop to clot and onward, as male or female and fortunate or wretched.
RAZI-FULL:v31p55#3/r1.anchor: قال الفراء : قدره أطوارا نطفة ثم علقة إلى آخر خلقه وذكرا أو أنثى

RAZI-FULL:v31p55#3/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p55#3/r2.speaker: الزجاج
RAZI-FULL:v31p55#3/r2.claim: Al-Zajjāj interprets it as forming the human upright, as in the account of creation in 18:37.
RAZI-FULL:v31p55#3/r2.anchor: قال الزجاج : المعنى قدره على الاستواء كما قال

RAZI-FULL:v31p55#3/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p55#3/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p55#3/r3.claim: Rāzī also allows that God set each organ's quantity and qualities in the proportions suited to its benefit.
RAZI-FULL:v31p55#3/r3.anchor: يحتمل أن يكون المراد وقدر كل عضو في الكمية والكيفية بالقدر اللائق بمصلحته

STUDYQURAN:80:18/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:80:18/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:80:18/r1.claim: Creation of the human from a drop is evidence of God's Omnipotence, as in other passages.
STUDYQURAN:80:18/r1.anchor: This is one of several passages in which the creation of the human being from a drop is cited as evidence of God’s Omnipotence

TAB-FULL:v24p111/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p111/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v24p111/r2.claim: God created and proportioned him through successive stages in the womb: a drop, then a clot, then a morsel of flesh and later stages.
TAB-FULL:v24p111/r2.anchor: فقال {من نطفة خلقه فقدره} [عبس: 19] أحوالا: نطفة تارة، ثم علقة أخرى، ثم مضغة

TABATABAI:80:17-19/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:80:17-19/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:80:17-19/r1.claim: The passage condemns human ingratitude and recalls that God creates, measures, guides, causes death, buries, and resurrects the human, who owns none of this governance.
TABATABAI:80:17-19/r1.anchor: بيان دعاء على الانسان وتعجيب من مبالغته في الكفر بربوبية ربه وإشارة إلى أمره حدوثا وبقاء فإنه لا يملك لنفسه شيئا

TABATABAI:80:17-19/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:80:17-19/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:80:17-19/r2.claim: Even food alone displays God's vast, subtle governance and immeasurable mercy; overlooking this care and failing to give thanks is astonishing human injustice and ingratitude.
TABATABAI:80:17-19/r2.anchor: ولو نظر الإنسان إلى طعامه فقط وهو مظهر واحد من مظاهر تدبيره وغرفة من بحار رحمته رأى من وسيع التدبير ولطيف الصنع

TABATABAI:80:17-19/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:80:17-19/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:80:17-19/r3.claim: These verses can continue the preceding passage as one context, although some commentators say they were revealed for a separate occasion discussed later.
TABATABAI:80:17-19/r3.anchor: لا تأبى الاتصال بما قبلها سياقا واحدا وإن قال بعضهم أنها نزلت لسبب آخر كما سيجيء

TABATABAI:80:19-20/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:80:19-20/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:80:19-20/r1.claim: The indefinite form of nutfa belittles it: the human was created from a lowly, insignificant drop, so he has no basis for arrogance or disobedience.
TABATABAI:80:19-20/r1.anchor: للتحقير أي من نطفة مهينة حقيرة خلقه فلا يحق له وأصله هذا الأصل أن يطغى

TABATABAI:80:19-20/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:80:19-20/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:80:19-20/r2.claim: God gave the human measure in essence, attributes, and acts; divine governance surrounds him, so he must not exceed his allotted nature or limits.
TABATABAI:80:19-20/r2.anchor: أعطاه القدر في ذاته وصفاته وأفعاله فليس له أن يتعدى الطور الذي قدر له ويتجاوز الحد

BURSEVI:v10p260/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p260/r8.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p260/r8.claim: A nutfa is a filthy, lowly drop; someone created from it has no basis for arrogance toward the benefactor who gave him a beautiful form.
BURSEVI:v10p260/r8.anchor: {من نطفة} قذرة {خلقه} فمن كان أصله مثل هذا الشيء الحقير كيف يليق به

BURSEVI:v10p260/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p260/r9.speaker: السجاوندي
BURSEVI:v10p260/r9.claim: Al-Sajāwandī pauses after from a drop, supplying another created him from what precedes and treating created him, then proportioned him as a new explanatory sentence.
BURSEVI:v10p260/r9.anchor: وقف السجاوندي على قوله من نطفة حتى وضع عليه علامة الوقف المطلق

BURSEVI:v10p260/r10.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p260/r10.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p260/r10.claim: The more apparent construction connects from a drop to created him and does not pause there; taking created him proportioned him as a new sentence avoids redundancy because creation itself entails measured quantities and qualities.
BURSEVI:v10p260/r10.anchor: ومن جعله متعلقا بما بعده على ما هو الظاهر لم يقف عليه

BURSEVI:v10p260/r11.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p260/r11.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p260/r11.claim: God prepared the human being with suitable organs, shapes, quantities, qualities, and capacities, each fitted to its benefit and proper use.
BURSEVI:v10p260/r11.anchor: فهيأه لما يصلح له ويليق به من الأعضاء والأشكال أي أحدثه بمقدار

BURSEVI:v10p260/r12.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p260/r12.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p260/r12.claim: Alternatively, proportioning describes development through successive stages, from a clot and a morsel of flesh to completion, as male or female and wretched or blessed.
BURSEVI:v10p260/r12.anchor: أو فقدره أطوار إلى أن تم خلقه فالتقدير المتفرع على الخلق مأخوذ

WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p222#2/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p222#2/r1.speaker: ابن عباس، مقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p222#2/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas and Muqatil say God determines the child in its mother’s womb.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p222#2/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p222#2/r2.speaker: الفراء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p222#2/r2.claim: Al-Farra says God shapes the human through stages from sperm to clot and onward, determining sex and whether the person is fortunate or wretched.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p222#2/r2.anchor: ما ذكره الفراء: وقدره أطوارا: نطفة، علقة إلى آخر خلقه

WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p222#2/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p222#2/r3.speaker: الزجاج
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p222#2/r3.claim: Al-Zajjaj reads it as proportioning the human into an upright form, comparing 18:37.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p222#2/r3.anchor: والثاني: ما ذكره الزجاج قال: المعنى: فقدره على الاستواء

WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p222#2/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p222#2/r4.speaker: الكلبي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p222#2/r4.claim: Al-Kalbi says God proportioned the body’s form, head, eyes, hands, and feet.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p222#2/r4.anchor: وهذا معنى قول الكلبي: (قدر خلقه، ورأسه، وعينيه

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:80:19/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:80:19/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:80:19/r1.claim: God proportioned the human through stages from a clot and morsel until birth from the mother’s womb.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:80:19/r1.anchor: أطوارا من علقة ومضغة إلى أن خرج من بطن أمه

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:80:17/r3.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:80:17/r3.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:80:17/r3.claim: By recalling how humans came into existence after nonexistence, the verses urge the deniers and anyone doubtful about resurrection to reflect and believe.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:80:17/r3.anchor: insanın hiç yokken varlık alanına nasıl çıkarıldığı hatırlatılmakta, böylece insanlar düşünme ve inanmaya teşvik edilmektedir

QUSHAYRI:v3p392/r24.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p392/r24.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p392/r24.claim: God created, formed, and proportioned the human being through successive stages: a drop, then a clot, then stage after stage.
QUSHAYRI:v3p392/r24.anchor: خلقه وصوره وقدره أطوارا : من نطفة ، ثم علقة ، ثم طورا بعد طور

BURHAN:v4p92/r4.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p92/r4.speaker: الزمخشري
BURHAN:v4p92/r4.claim: Al-Zamakhshari says the question belittles the human origin as something low and contemptible, then identifies it as a drop of semen.
BURHAN:v4p92/r4.anchor: قال الزمخشري أي ( 7 ) من شئ حقير مهين ثم بينه

ITQAN:v2p556/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p556/r6.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p556/r6.claim: An indefinite may belittle: the question 'from what thing?' points to man's lowly origin, then specifies a drop of fluid.
ITQAN:v2p556/r6.anchor: ﴿ من أي شيء خلقه ﴾ أي من شيء حقير مهين ثم بينه بقوله ﴿ من نطفة خلقه ﴾

FARRA:v3p237/r1.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v3p237/r1.speaker: author
FARRA:v3p237/r1.claim: The question is answered by his origin as a sperm, then a clot and subsequent stages; God decreed his outcome as wretched or blessed and male or female.

NAHHAS:v5p151/r4.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p151/r4.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v5p151/r4.claim: Humans are created from something lowly and become noble through obedience to God.
NAHHAS:v5p151/r4.anchor: أي وإنما خلق من قذر وإنما ينبل بطاعة الله

ZAJJAJ:v5p284/r5.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p284/r5.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p284/r5.claim: Faqaddarahu means God proportioned him properly, as another verse says He fashioned a person from dust, then a drop, and made him a man.
ZAJJAJ:v5p284/r5.anchor: المعنى فقدره على الاستواء كما قال عز وجل: (أكفرت بالذي خلقك من تراب ثم من نطفة ثم سواك رجلا

ASAD-NOTES:80:17#n6/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:80:17#n6/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:80:17#n6/r1.claim: Asad explains that human nature is determined for the organic roles of body and mind and for adapting to natural conditions.
ASAD-NOTES:80:17#n6/r1.anchor: organic functions which man's body and mind are to fulfil, and the natural conditions

ASAD-NOTES:80:17#n6/r2.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:80:17#n6/r2.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:80:17#n6/r2.claim: Although verses 18–22 use the past tense, Asad says they describe a recurring phenomenon.
ASAD-NOTES:80:17#n6/r2.anchor: Verses 18-22, although formulated in the past tense, obviously describe a recurrent phenomenon.

ALUSI-FULL:v30p44#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p44#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p44#2/r1.claim: The answer is not literal: it takes the form of an answer and is appositional to the preceding question; alternatively, it serves for emphasis, with belittlement conveyed by the indefinite ‘thing’ or by ‘drop.’
ALUSI-FULL:v30p44#2/r1.anchor: لا يقتضي أنه حقيقي لأنه ليس بجواب في الحقيقة بل على صورته وهو بدل من قوله سبحانه من أي شيء خلقه

ALUSI-FULL:v30p44#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p44#2/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p44#2/r2.claim: The human was created from a vile, humble drop.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p44#2/r2.anchor: أي من أي شيء حقير مهين خلقه من نطفة مذرة

ALUSI-FULL:v30p44#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p44#2/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p44#2/r3.claim: God fashioned the human with suitable limbs and forms; here qaddara means preparing and fitting him for what suits him, so the sequence with fa is apt.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p44#2/r3.anchor: فهيأه لما يصلح له ويليق به من الأعضاء والأشكال فالتقدير بمعنى التهيئة لما يصلح

ALUSI-FULL:v30p44#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p44#2/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p44#2/r4.claim: Alternatively, this elaborates the earlier summary: God developed him through stages until his creation was complete.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p44#2/r4.anchor: وجوز أن يكون هذا تفصيلا لما أجمل أولا في قوله تعالى من أي شيء خلقه أي فقدره أطوار إلى أن أتم خلقه

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p337/r11.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p337/r11.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p337/r11.claim: The person passes through stages, from a sperm drop to a clot and onward through the rest of creation.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p337/r11.anchor: من نطفة خلقه فقدره} أطوارا: نطفة ثم علقة إلى آخر خلقه،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p337/r12.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p337/r12.speaker: الكلبي
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p337/r12.claim: Al-Kalbi says God measured the person's creation, including head, eyes, hands, and feet.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p337/r12.anchor: قال الكلبي: قدر خلقه، رأسه وعينيه ويديه ورجليه.

BAYDAWI-FULL:80:17-20/r6.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:80:17-20/r6.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:80:17-20/r6.claim: God prepared the person for fitting organs and forms, or determined his successive developmental stages until his creation was complete.
BAYDAWI-FULL:80:17-20/r6.anchor: فهيأه لما يصلح له من الأعضاء والأشكال،

BIQAI-FULL:v8p328/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p328/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p328/r3.claim: Because denial of the Resurrection is the main issue, the argument turns to the human being’s origin, contrasting lowly beginnings with the honor God later gives.

BIQAI-FULL:v8p328/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p328/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p328/r5.claim: God creates the human from a very small quantity of fluid, forms it, and prepares its outward and inward organs, shapes, and developmental stages.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p328/r5.anchor: ماء يسير جدا لا من غيره

BIQAI-FULL:v8p328/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p328/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p328/r6.claim: The three darknesses may be the belly, womb, and placenta.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p328/r6.anchor: ثم جعله في ظلمات ثلاث : ظلمة البطن ثم الرحمن ثم المشيمة

BIQAI-FULL:v8p328/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p328/r7.speaker: أهل التشريح
BIQAI-FULL:v8p328/r7.claim: Anatomists identify the three darknesses as three membranes: the placenta feeds the fetus through the navel, while the others receive urine and bodily vapors.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p328/r7.anchor: أو هي على ما قال أهل التشريح ثلاثة أغشية : أحدها المشيمة تتصل بسرة الجنين تمده بالغذاء

BIQAI-FULL:v8p328/r14.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p328/r14.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p328/r14.claim: Humanity begins as filthy fluid and ends as a foul corpse, carrying excrement in between; only the Creator granted knowledge and honor, so the response should be gratitude, not disbelief.

DURR-FULL:v8p418/r11.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p418/r11.speaker: ابن جريج
DURR-FULL:v8p418/r11.claim: Ibn Jurayj says God determined the human through successive stages, from a drop to a clot and morsel until formation was complete.
DURR-FULL:v8p418/r11.anchor: وفي قوله: {فقدره} قال: نطفة ثم علقة ثم مضغة ثم كذا

DURR-FULL:v8p418/r12.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p418/r12.speaker: عكرمة
DURR-FULL:v8p418/r12.claim: Ikrima says God determined the person’s form and course as He willed in the mother’s womb.
DURR-FULL:v8p418/r12.anchor: وأخرج عبد بن حميد وابن المنذر عن عكرمة في قوله: {خلقه فقدره} قال: قدره في رحم أمه كيف شاء

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p122/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p122/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p122/r1.claim: The question-and-answer arrangement builds anticipation, like the earlier question about the great news.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p122/r1.anchor: وجيء في هذا الاستدلال بصورة سؤال وجواب للتشويق إلى مضمونه ، ولذلك قرن الاستفهام بالجواب عنه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p122/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p122/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p122/r2.claim: The question is formal: it asks what substance formed the human, not whether God created him; its point is to establish the possibility of recreating him by analogy with the first creation.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p122/r2.anchor: والاستفهام صوري ، وجعل المستفهم عنه تعيين الأمر الذي به خلق الإنسان لأن المقام هنا ليس لإثبات أن الله خلق الإنسان

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p122/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p122/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p122/r4.claim: The answer front-loads ‘from a sperm-drop’ to echo the question and emphasize the source, alerting listeners to God’s wisdom in making the wondrous creature from a simple material.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p122/r4.anchor: وقدم الجار والمجرور في قوله : { من نطفة خلقه } محاكاة لتقديم المبين في السؤال الذي اقتضى تقديمه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p122/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p122/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p122/r5.claim: Repeating ‘He created him’ despite the question’s verb draws attention to the precision of this remarkable creation.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p122/r5.anchor: وإنما لم يستغن عن إعادة فعل خلقه في جملة الجواب مع العلم به بتقدم ذكر حاصله في السؤال لزيادة التنبيه على دقة ذلك الخلق البديع .

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p122/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p122/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p122/r6.claim: The second ‘created him’ is balanced expression, neither ellipsis nor verbosity.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p122/r6.anchor: فذكر فعل { خلقه } الثاني من أسلوب المساواة ليس بإيجاز ، وليس بإطناب .

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p122/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p122/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p122/r7.claim: Nuṭfa means a small quantity of water; its pattern is a passive noun, like a handful of grain or scoop of water, and its common usage is reproductive fluid.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p122/r7.anchor: والنطفة : الماء القليل ، وهي فعلة بمعنى مفعولة كقولهم : قبضة حب ، وغرفة ماء .

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p122/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p122/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p122/r8.claim: Mentioning reproductive fluid as the material of animal creation shows God’s wondrous making and the possibility of resurrection; it does not demean human origins, since the focus is great creation rather than rebuking arrogance.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p122/r8.anchor: فذكرت النطفة لتعين ذكرها لأنها مادة خلق الحيوان للدلالة على أن صنع الله بديع فإمكان البعث حاصل

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p123/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p123/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p123/r1.claim: The fāʾ makes measuring a consequence of creating; taqdīr is bringing something into being according to a precise, ordered measure.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p123/r1.anchor: وفرع على فعل { خلقه } فعل { فقدره } بفاء التفريع لأن التقدير هنا إيجاد الشيء على مقدار مضبوط منظم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p123/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p123/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p123/r2.claim: God made the human ready for growth and attendant faculties, intellect and agency, enabling reflection and chosen acts through gradual development.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p123/r2.anchor: أي جعل التقدير من آثار الخلق لأنه خلقه متهيئا للنماء وما يلابسه من العقل والتصرف وتمكينه من النظر بعقله

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p123/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p123/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p123/r3.claim: This sequence also embeds a reminder of divine beneficence within the argument.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p123/r3.anchor: وهذا التفريع وما عطف عليه إدماج للامتنان في خلال الاستدلال .

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p138#20/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p138#20/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p138#20/r3.claim: Putting “from a drop” first echoes the question’s fronted phrase and highlights the source of creation as proof of God’s wisdom: the wondrous human comes from something slight.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p138#20/r3.anchor: وقدم الجار والمجرور في قوله : { من نطفة خلقه } محاكاة لتقديم المبين في السؤال الذي اقتضى تقديمه كونه استفهاما يستحق صدر الكلام

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p138#20/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p138#20/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p138#20/r4.claim: The answer repeats “He created him” although the verb is understood, to emphasize the precision of the wondrous creation; the repetition is balanced, neither omission nor excess.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p138#20/r4.anchor: وإنما لم يستغن عن إعادة فعل خلقه في جملة الجواب مع العلم به بتقدم ذكر حاصله في السؤال لزيادة التنبيه على دقة ذلك الخلق البديع .

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p138#20/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p138#20/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p138#20/r5.claim: Nuṭfa means a small amount of water; its pattern is a passive noun, like qubḍa (a handful) and ghurfa (a scoop).
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p138#20/r5.anchor: والنطفة : الماء القليل ، وهي فعلة بمعنى مفعولة كقولهم : قبضة حب ، وغرفة ماء .

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p138#20/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p138#20/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p138#20/r6.claim: The word came to denote the reproductive fluid, the material from which animals are created.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p138#20/r6.anchor: وغلب إطلاق النطفة على الماء الذي منه التناسل ، فذكرت النطفة لتعين ذكرها لأنها مادة خلق الحيوان

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p138#20/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p138#20/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p138#20/r7.claim: Mentioning the drop demonstrates the wonder of God’s creation and the possibility of resurrection; it is not meant to demean humanity’s origin, since the context concerns creation’s greatness, not rebuking pride.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p138#20/r7.anchor: للدلالة على أن صنع الله بديع فإمكان البعث حاصل ، وليس في ذكر النطفة هنا إيماء إلى تحقير أصل نشأة الإنسان

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p138#20/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p138#20/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p138#20/r8.claim: Qaddara here means bringing something into existence in a precise, ordered measure.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p138#20/r8.anchor: لأن التقدير هنا إيجاد الشيء على مقدار مضبوط منظم كقوله تعالى : { وخلق كل شيء فقدره تقديرا }

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p138#20/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p138#20/r9.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p138#20/r9.claim: The fāʾ marks a consequence: measure is an effect of creation, which equips the human to grow, reason, act, and exercise judgment.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p138#20/r9.anchor: وفرع على فعل { خلقه } فعل { فقدره } بفاء التفريع لأن التقدير هنا إيجاد الشيء على مقدار مضبوط منظم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p438#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p438#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p438#2/r3.claim: The indicated substance is the man’s fluid and the woman’s fluid.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p438#2/r3.anchor: واللفظ المشار إليه ماء الرجل وماء المرأة،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p438#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p438#2/r4.speaker: جمهور الناس
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p438#2/r4.claim: The majority read فقدّره with doubled dāl.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p438#2/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p438#2/r5.speaker: بعض القراء
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p438#2/r5.claim: Some readers pronounce the dāl without doubling.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p438#2/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p438#2/r6.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p438#2/r6.claim: God apportioned each person’s body, organs, lifespan, and other aspects as He willed.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p438#2/r6.anchor: جعله بقدر واحد معلوم من الأعضاء والخلق والأجل وغير ذلك من أنحائه حسب إرادته تعالى

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p31#2/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p31#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p31#2/r1.claim: The human was created from a sperm drop.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p31#2/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p31#2/r2.speaker: ابن السائب
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p31#2/r2.claim: Ibn al-Sāʾib says God proportioned his body parts, including head, eyes, hands, and feet.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p31#2/r2.anchor: أحدها قدر أعضاءه رأسه وعينيه ويديه ورجليه قاله ابن السائب

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p31#2/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p31#2/r3.speaker: مقاتل
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p31#2/r3.claim: Muqātil says God assigned him successive stages, from sperm to clot and onward through creation.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p31#2/r3.anchor: والثاني قدره أطوارا نطفة ثم علقه إلى آخر خلقه قاله مقاتل

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p31#2/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p31#2/r4.speaker: الزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p31#2/r4.claim: Al-Zajjāj interprets the phrase as making him well proportioned.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p31#2/r4.anchor: والثالث فقدره على الاستواء قاله الزجاج

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p322#3/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p322#3/r6.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p322#3/r6.claim: God reminds the person of creation from a lowly drop and of the destiny He apportioned—lifespan, provision, deeds, and whether one is wretched or blessed—as proof He can recreate him.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p322#3/r6.anchor: أي: قدر أجله ورزقه وعمله وشقي أو سعيد.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p703#2/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p703#2/r5.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p703#2/r5.claim: God created the human from a drop of fluid and then measured and prepared him for what suits and distinguishes him.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p703#2/r5.anchor: فهيأه لما يصلح له ويختص به

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p703#2/r6.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p703#2/r6.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p703#2/r6.claim: This measured creation recalls the statement that God created everything and determined it precisely.

MUQATIL:80:18-23/r2.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:80:18-23/r2.speaker: author
MUQATIL:80:18-23/r2.claim: The embryo develops in the womb from a drop to a clot, then a lump, bones, and finally a spirit; God determines its form before birth.
MUQATIL:80:18-23/r2.anchor: في بطن أمه من نطفة، ثم من عقلة، ثم من مضغة، ثم عظما، ثم روحا

NASAFI-FULL:v4p317#17/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p317#17/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p317#17/r1.claim: God created him from a drop and proportioned him according to what He willed for his creation.

QURTUBI-FULL:80:17-19/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:80:17-19/r10.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:80:17-19/r10.claim: He was created from a small, base, lifeless quantity of fluid; why, then, is he deceived about himself?
QURTUBI-FULL:80:17-19/r10.anchor: { من نطفة } أي من ماء يسير مهين جماد { خلقه } فلم يغلط في نفسه

QURTUBI-FULL:80:17-19/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:80:17-19/r11.speaker: الحسن
QURTUBI-FULL:80:17-19/r11.claim: Al-Hasan asks how one can be arrogant when one came out twice from the passage of urine.
QURTUBI-FULL:80:17-19/r11.anchor: قال الحسن: كيف يتكبر من خرج من سبيل البول مرتين

QURTUBI-FULL:80:17-19/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:80:17-19/r12.speaker: الضحاك عن ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:80:17-19/r12.claim: Al-Dahhak reports from Ibn Abbas that God determined the fetus's hands, feet, eyes and other parts, beauty or ugliness, height, and whether it would be wretched or fortunate.
QURTUBI-FULL:80:17-19/r12.anchor: كذا روى الضحاك عن ابن عباس: أي قدر يديه ورجليه وعينيه وسائر آرابه، وحسنا ودميما، وقصيرا وطويلا

QURTUBI-FULL:80:17-19/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:80:17-19/r13.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:80:17-19/r13.claim: Another gloss takes qaddarahu to mean proportioned him, as in the parallels cited from al-Kahf and al-Infitar.

QURTUBI-FULL:80:19-20/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:80:19-20/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:80:19-20/r1.claim: Another explanation is that God determined the human in stages, from a drop to a clot until his creation was complete.
QURTUBI-FULL:80:19-20/r1.anchor: وقيل: «فقدره» أطوارا أي من حال إلى حال نطفة ثم علقة، إلى أن تم خلقه

TABRISI:80:20#2/r23.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:80:20#2/r23.speaker: author
TABRISI:80:20#2/r23.claim: God formed the human through successive stages, then proportioned his stature, senses, limbs, lifespan, provision, and all his circumstances.
TABRISI:80:20#2/r23.anchor: { من نطفة خلقه فقدره } أطوارا نطفة ثم علقة إلى آخر خلقه وعلى حد من طوله وقصره وسمعه وبصره
